sentences.text: Oraristrix brea likely had more terrestrial habits than modern North American owls of the genera Bubo and Strix, indicated by its relatively long legs compared to its wingspan.
Oraristrix brea, the La Brea owl, is an extinct owl found in the Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits of the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, California.
The species was first described by Hildegarde Howard in 1933 as Strix brea before being moved to the genus Oraristrix by Campbell and Bocheński in 2010.
Fossils of this species have also been found in Upper Pleistocene asphalt deposits at Carpinteria, California.
Oraristrix belongs to the family Strigidae.
Oraristrix lived from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
